Definition: of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet); "iota", the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put (figuratively) for a very small part of anything:--jot.
BiblicalUsage: An iota is the smallest letter of the alphabet, and Jesus stakes everything on it. In Matthew 5:18 he says, till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the smallest letter is the surest thing in the Bible: not one stroke of God's word will fail.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
